Detachments of Hypergraphs I: The Berge-Johnson Problem

Amin Bahmanian Address: Department of Mathematics and Statistics Auburn University, Auburn, AL USA 36849-5310 Email address: mzb0004@tigermail.auburn.edu
Date: August 24, 2026
Abstract.

A detachment of a hypergraph is formed by splitting each vertex into one or more subvertices, and sharing the incident edges arbitrarily among the subvertices. For a given edge-colored hypergraph ℱ\mathscr{F}, we prove that there exists a detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} such that the degree of each vertex and the multiplicity of each edge in ℱ\mathscr{F} (and each color class of ℱ\mathscr{F}) are shared fairly among the subvertices in 𝒢\mathscr{G} (and each color class of 𝒢\mathscr{G}, respectively).

Let (λ1​…,λm)​Kp1,…,pnh1,…,hm(\lambda_{1}\dots,\lambda_{m})K^{h_{1},\dots,h_{m}}_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}} be a hypergraph with vertex partition {V1,…,Vn}\{V_{1},\dots,V_{n}\}, |Vi|=pi|V_{i}|=p_{i} for 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n such that there are λi\lambda_{i} edges of size hih_{i} incident with every hih_{i} vertices, at most one vertex from each part for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m (so no edge is incident with more than one vertex of a part). We use our detachment theorem to show that the obvious necessary conditions for (λ1​…,λm)​Kp1,…,pnh1,…,hm(\lambda_{1}\dots,\lambda_{m})K^{h_{1},\dots,h_{m}}_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}} to be expressed as the union 𝒢1∪…∪𝒢k\mathscr{G}_{1}\cup\ldots\cup\mathscr{G}_{k} of kk edge-disjoint factors, where for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 𝒢i\mathscr{G}_{i} is rir_{i}-regular, are also sufficient. Baranyai solved the case of h1=⋯=hmh_{1}=\dots=h_{m}, λ1=…,λm=1\lambda_{1}=\dots,\lambda_{m}=1, p1=⋯=pmp_{1}=\dots=p_{m}, r1=⋯=rkr_{1}=\dots=r_{k}. Berge and Johnson, (and later Brouwer and Tijdeman, respectively) considered (and solved, respectively) the case of hi=ih_{i}=i, 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, p1=⋯=pm=λ1=⋯=λm=r1=⋯=rk=1p_{1}=\dots=p_{m}=\lambda_{1}=\dots=\lambda_{m}=r_{1}=\dots=r_{k}=1. We also extend our result to the case where each 𝒢i\mathscr{G}_{i} is almost regular.

Key words and phrases: 
Amalgamations, Detachments, Factorization, Edge-coloring, Hypergraphs, Decomposition

1. Introduction

Intuitively speaking, a detachment of a hypergraph is formed by splitting each vertex into one or more subvertices, and sharing the incident edges arbitrarily among the subvertices. As the main result of this paper (see Theorem 4.1), we prove that for a given edge-colored hypergraph ℱ\mathscr{F}, there exists a detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} such that the degree of each vertex and the multiplicity of each edge in ℱ\mathscr{F} (and each color class of ℱ\mathscr{F}) are shared fairly among the subvertices in 𝒢\mathscr{G} (and each color class of 𝒢\mathscr{G}, respectively). This result is not only interesting by itself and generalizes various graph theoretic results (see for example [1, 10, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19]), but also is used to obtain extensions of existing results on edge-decompositions of hypergraphs by Bermond, Baranyai [2, 3], Berge and Johnson [4, 13], and Brouwer and Tijdeman [5, 6].

Given a set NN of nn elements, Berge and Johnson [4, 13] addressed the question of when do there exist disjoint partitions of NN, each partition containing only subsets of hh or fewer elements, such that every subset of NN having hh or fewer elements is in exactly one partition. Here we state the problem in a more general setting with the hypergraph theoretic notation.

Let (λ1​…,λm)​Kp1,…,pnh1,…,hm(\lambda_{1}\dots,\lambda_{m})K^{h_{1},\dots,h_{m}}_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}} be a hypergraph with vertex partition {V1,…,Vn}\{V_{1},\dots,V_{n}\}, |Vi|=pi|V_{i}|=p_{i} for 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n such that there are λi\lambda_{i} edges of size hih_{i} incident with every hih_{i} vertices, at most one vertex from each part for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m (so no edge is incident with more than one vertex of a part). We use our detachment theorem to show that the obvious necessary conditions for (λ1​…,λm)​Kp1,…,pnh1,…,hm(\lambda_{1}\dots,\lambda_{m})K^{h_{1},\dots,h_{m}}_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}} to be expressed as the union 𝒢1∪…∪𝒢k\mathscr{G}_{1}\cup\ldots\cup\mathscr{G}_{k} of kk edge-disjoint factors, where for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 𝒢i\mathscr{G}_{i} is rir_{i}-regular, are also sufficient. Baranyai [2, 3] solved the case of h1=⋯=hmh_{1}=\dots=h_{m}, λ1=…,λm=1\lambda_{1}=\dots,\lambda_{m}=1, p1=⋯=pmp_{1}=\dots=p_{m}, r1=⋯=rkr_{1}=\dots=r_{k}. Berge and Johnson [4, 13], (and later Brouwer and Tijdeman [5, 6], respectively) considered (and solved, respectively) the case of hi=ih_{i}=i, 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, p1=⋯=pm=λ1=⋯=λm=r1=⋯=rk=1p_{1}=\dots=p_{m}=\lambda_{1}=\dots=\lambda_{m}=r_{1}=\dots=r_{k}=1. We also extend our result to the case where each 𝒢i\mathscr{G}_{i} is almost regular.

In the next two sections, we give more precise definitions along with terminology. In Section 4, we state our main result, followed by the proof in Section 5. In the last section, we show the usefulness of the main result on decompositions of various classes of hypergraphs. We defer the applications of the main result in solving embedding problems to a future paper.

2. Terminology and precise definitions

If x,y∈ℝx,y\in\mathbb{R} (ℝ\mathbb{R} is the set of real numbers), then ⌊x⌋\lfloor x\rfloor and ⌈x⌉\lceil x\rceil denote the integers such that x−1<⌊x⌋≤x≤⌈x⌉<x+1x-1<\lfloor x\rfloor\leq x\leq\lceil x\rceil<x+1, and x≈yx\approx y means ⌊y⌋≤x≤⌈y⌉\lfloor y\rfloor\leq x\leq\lceil y\rceil. We observe that the relation ≈\approx is transitive (but not symmetric) and for x,y∈ℝx,y\in\mathbb{R}, and n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N} (ℕ\mathbb{N} is the set of positive integers), x≈yx\approx y implies x/n≈y/nx/n\approx y/n. These properties of ≈\approx will be used in Section 5 without further explanation. For a multiset AA and u∈Au\in A, let μA​(u)\mu_{A}(u) denote the multiplicity of uu in AA, and let |A|=∑u∈AμA​(u)|A|=\sum_{u\in A}\mu_{A}(u). For multisets A1,…,AnA_{1},\dots,A_{n}, we define A=⋃i=1nAiA=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}A_{i} by μA​(u)=∑i=1nμAi​(u)\mu_{A}(u)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mu_{A_{i}}(u). We may use abbreviations such as {ur}\{u^{r}\} for {u,…,u⏟r}\{{\underbrace{u,\ldots,u}_{r}}\} — for example {u2,v,w2}∪{u,w2}={u3,v,w4}\{u^{2},v,w^{2}\}\cup\{u,w^{2}\}=\{u^{3},v,w^{4}\}.

For the purpose of this paper, a hypergraph 𝒢\mathscr{G} is an ordered quintuple (V⁡(𝒢),E⁡(𝒢),H⁡(𝒢)CLOSE,(V(\mathscr{G}),E(\mathscr{G}),H(\mathscr{G}), OPENψ,ϕ)\psi,\phi) where V⁡(𝒢),E⁡(𝒢),H⁡(𝒢)V(\mathscr{G}),E(\mathscr{G}),H(\mathscr{G}) are disjoint finite sets, ψ:H⁡(𝒢)→V⁡(𝒢)\psi:H(\mathscr{G})\rightarrow V(\mathscr{G}) is a function and ϕ:H⁡(𝒢)→E⁡(𝒢)\phi:H(\mathscr{G})\rightarrow E(\mathscr{G}) is a surjection. Elements of V⁡(𝒢),E⁡(𝒢),H⁡(𝒢)V(\mathscr{G}),E(\mathscr{G}),H(\mathscr{G}) are called vertices, edges and hinges of 𝒢\mathscr{G}, respectively. A vertex vv (edge ee, respectively) and hinge hh are said to be incident with each other if ψ⁡(h)=v\psi(h)=v (ϕ⁡(h)=e\phi(h)=e, respectively). A hinge hh is said to attach the edge ϕ⁡(h)\phi(h) to the vertex ψ⁡(h)\psi(h). In this manner, the vertex ψ⁡(h)\psi(h) and the edge ϕ⁡(h)\phi(h) are said to be incident with each other. If e∈E⁡(𝒢)e\in E(\mathscr{G}), and ee is incident with nn hinges h1,…,hnh_{1},\ldots,h_{n} for some n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}, then the edge ee is said to join (not necessarily distinct) vertices ψ⁡(h1),…,ψ⁡(hn)\psi(h_{1}),\ldots,\psi(h_{n}). If v∈V⁡(𝒢)v\in V(\mathscr{G}), then the number of hinges incident with vv (i.e. |ψ−1​(v)||\psi^{-1}(v)|) is called the degree of vv and is denoted by d⁡(v)d(v). The number of (distinct) vertices incident with an edge ee, denoted by |e||e|, is called the size of ee. If for all edges ee of 𝒢\mathscr{G}, |e|≤2|e|\leq 2 and |ϕ−1​(e)|=2|\phi^{-1}(e)|=2, then 𝒢\mathscr{G} is a graph.

Thus a hypergraph, in the sense of our definition, is a generalization of a hypergraph as it is usually defined. In fact, if for every edge ee, |e|=|ϕ−1​(e)||e|=|\phi^{-1}(e)|, then our definition is essentially the same as the usual definition. Here for convenience, we imagine each edge of a hypergraph to be attached to the vertices which it joins by in-between objects called hinges. Readers from a graph theory background may think of this as a bipartite multigraph with vertex bipartition {V,E}\{V,E\}, in which the hinges form the edges. A hypergraph may be drawn as a set of points representing the vertices. A hyperedge is represented by a simple closed curve enclosing its incident vertices. A hinge is represented by a small line attached to the vertex incident with it (see Figure 1).

The set of hinges of 𝒢\mathscr{G} which are incident with a vertex vv (and an edge ee, respectively), is denoted by H⁡(v)H(v) (H⁡(v,e)H(v,e), respectively). Thus if v∈V⁡(𝒢)v\in V(\mathscr{G}), then H​(v)=ψ−1​(v)H(v)=\psi^{-1}(v), and |H⁡(v)||H(v)| is the degree d⁡(v)d(v) of vv. If UU is a multi-subset of V⁡(𝒢)V(\mathscr{G}), and u∈V⁡(𝒢)u\in V(\mathscr{G}), let E⁡(U)E(U) denote the set of edges ee with |ϕ−1​(e)|=|U||\phi^{-1}(e)|=|U| joining vertices in UU. More precisely, E(U)={e∈E(𝒢)| for all v∈V(𝒢),|H(v,e)|=μU(v)}E(U)=\{e\in E(\mathscr{G})|\mbox{ for all }v\in V(\mathscr{G}),|H(v,e)|=\mu_{U}(v)\}. For U1,…,Un⊂VU_{1},\dots,U_{n}\subset V where for 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n each UiU_{i} is a multiset, let E⁡(U1,…,Un)E(U_{1},\dots,U_{n}) denote E⁡(⋃i=1nUi)E(\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}U_{i}). We write m⁡(U)m(U) for |E⁡(U)||E(U)| and call it the multiplicity of UU. For simplicity, E⁡(ur,U)E(u^{r},U) denotes E⁡({ur},U)E(\{u^{r}\},U), and m⁡(u1m1,…,urmr)m(u_{1}^{m_{1}},\dots,u_{r}^{m_{r}}) denotes m⁡({u1m1,…,urmr})m(\{u_{1}^{m_{1}},\dots,u_{r}^{m_{r}}\}). The set of hinges that are incident with uu and an edge in E⁡(ur,U)E(u^{r},U) is denoted by H⁡(ur,U)H(u^{r},U).

    m⁡(v1,v2,v3)=0,m⁡(v12,v2,v3)=1m(v_{1},v_{2},v_{3})=0,m(v_{1}^{2},v_{2},v_{3})=1,

    H⁡(v12,{v2,v3})={h1,h2},H⁡(v1,{v2,v3})=∅,H⁡(v3,{v12,v2})={h4}H(v_{1}^{2},\{v_{2},v_{3}\})=\{h_{1},h_{2}\},H(v_{1},\{v_{2},v_{3}\})=\varnothing,H(v_{3},\{v_{1}^{2},v_{2}\})=\{h_{4}\}.

A k-edge-coloring of 𝒢\mathscr{G} is a mapping f:E⁡(𝒢)→Cf:E(\mathscr{G})\rightarrow C, where CC is a set of kk colors (often we use C={1,…,k}C=\{1,\ldots,k\}), and the edges of one color form a color class. The sub-hypergraph of 𝒢\mathscr{G} induced by the color class jj is denoted by 𝒢⁡(j)\mathscr{G}(j). To avoid ambiguity, subscripts may be used to indicate the hypergraph in which hypergraph-theoretic notation should be interpreted — for example, d𝒢​(v)d_{\mathscr{G}}(v), E𝒢​(v2,w)E_{\mathscr{G}}(v^{2},w), H𝒢​(v)H_{\mathscr{G}}(v).

3. Amalgamations and detachments

If ℱ=(V,E,H,ψ,ϕ)\mathscr{F}=(V,E,H,\psi,\phi) is a hypergraph and Ψ\Psi is a function from VV onto a set WW, then we shall say that the hypergraph 𝒢=(W,E,H,Ψ∘ψ,ϕ)\mathscr{G}=(W,E,H,\Psi\circ\psi,\phi) is an amalgamation of ℱ\mathscr{F} and that ℱ\mathscr{F} is a detachment of 𝒢\mathscr{G}. Associated with Ψ\Psi is the number function g:W→ℕg:W\rightarrow\mathbb{N} defined by g​(w)=|Ψ−1​(w)|g(w)=|\Psi^{-1}(w)|, for each w∈Ww\in W; being more specific, we may also say that ℱ\mathscr{F} is a g-detachment of 𝒢\mathscr{G}. Intuitively speaking, a gg-detachment of 𝒢\mathscr{G} is obtained by splitting each u∈V⁡(𝒢)u\in V(\mathscr{G}) into g⁡(u)g(u) vertices. Thus ℱ\mathscr{F} and 𝒢\mathscr{G} have the same edges and hinges, and each vertex vv of 𝒢\mathscr{G} is obtained by identifying those vertices of ℱ\mathscr{F} which belong to the set Ψ−1​(v)\Psi^{-1}(v). In this process, a hinge incident with a vertex uu and an edge ee in ℱ\mathscr{F} becomes incident with the vertex Ψ⁡(u)\Psi(u) and the edge ee in 𝒢\mathscr{G}.

There are quite a lot of other papers on amalgamations and some highlights include [7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 18, 19].

4. Main Result

A function g:V⁡(𝒢)→ℕg:V(\mathscr{G})\rightarrow{\mathbb{N}} is said to be simple if

|H⁡(v,e)|≤g⁡(v)​ for ​v∈V⁡(𝒢),e∈E⁡(𝒢).|H(v,e)|\leq g(v)\mbox{ for }v\in V(\mathscr{G}),e\in E(\mathscr{G}).

A hypergraph 𝒢\mathscr{G} is said to be simple if g:V⁡(𝒢)→ℕg:V(\mathscr{G})\rightarrow{\mathbb{N}} with g⁡(v)=1g(v)=1 for v∈V⁡(𝒢)v\in V(\mathscr{G}) is simple. It is clear that for a hypergraph ℱ\mathscr{F} and a function g:V⁡(ℱ)→ℕg:V(\mathscr{F})\rightarrow{\mathbb{N}}, there exists a simple gg-detachment if and only if gg is simple.

Theorem 4.1.

Let ℱ\mathscr{F} be a kk-edge-colored hypergraph and let g:V⁡(ℱ)→ℕg:V(\mathscr{F})\rightarrow{\mathbb{N}} be a simple function. Then there exists a simple gg-detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} (possibly with multiple edges) of ℱ\mathscr{F} with amalgamation function Ψ:V⁡(𝒢)→V⁡(ℱ)\Psi:V(\mathscr{G})\rightarrow V(\mathscr{F}), gg being the number function associated with Ψ\Psi, such that:

  • (A1)

    d𝒢​(v)≈dℱ​(u)/g⁡(u)d_{\mathscr{G}}(v)\approx d_{\mathscr{F}}(u)/g(u) for each u∈V⁡(ℱ)u\in V(\mathscr{F}) and each v∈Ψ−1​(u);v\in\Psi^{-1}(u);

  • (A2)

    d𝒢⁡(j)​(v)≈dℱ⁡(j)​(u)/g⁡(u)d_{\mathscr{G}(j)}(v)\approx d_{\mathscr{F}(j)}(u)/g(u) for each u∈V⁡(ℱ)u\in V(\mathscr{F}), each v∈Ψ−1​(u)v\in\Psi^{-1}(u) and 1≤j≤k;1\leq j\leq k;

  • (A3)

    m𝒢​(U1,…,Ur)≈mℱ​(u1m1,…,urmr)/Πi=1r​(g⁡(ui)mi)m_{\mathscr{G}}(U_{1},\dots,U_{r})\approx m_{\mathscr{F}}(u_{1}^{m_{1}},\dots,u_{r}^{m_{r}})/\Pi_{i=1}^{r}\binom{g(u_{i})}{m_{i}} for distinct u1,…,ur∈V⁡(ℱ)u_{1},\dots,u_{r}\in V(\mathscr{F}) and Ui⊂Ψ−1​(ui)U_{i}\subset\Psi^{-1}(u_{i}) with |Ui|=mi≤g⁡(ui)|U_{i}|=m_{i}\leq g(u_{i}) for 1≤i≤r;1\leq i\leq r;

  • (A4)

    m𝒢⁡(j)​(U1,…,Ur)≈mℱ⁡(j)​(u1m1,…,urmr)/Πi=1r​(g⁡(ui)mi)m_{\mathscr{G}(j)}(U_{1},\dots,U_{r})\approx m_{\mathscr{F}(j)}(u_{1}^{m_{1}},\dots,u_{r}^{m_{r}})/\Pi_{i=1}^{r}\binom{g(u_{i})}{m_{i}} for distinct u1,…,ur∈V⁡(ℱ)u_{1},\dots,u_{r}\in V(\mathscr{F}) and Ui⊂Ψ−1​(ui)U_{i}\subset\Psi^{-1}(u_{i}) with |Ui|=mi≤g⁡(ui)|U_{i}|=m_{i}\leq g(u_{i}) for 1≤i≤r1\leq i\leq r and 1≤j≤k.1\leq j\leq k.

A family 𝒜\mathscr{A} of sets is laminar if, for every pair A,BA,B of sets belonging to 𝒜\mathscr{A}, either A⊂BA\subset B, or B⊂AB\subset A, or A∩B=∅A\cap B=\varnothing. To prove the main result, we need the following lemma:

Lemma 4.2.

(Nash-Williams [18, Lemma 2]) If 𝒜,ℬ\mathscr{A},\mathscr{B} are two laminar families of subsets of a finite set SS, and n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}, then there exist a subset AA of SS such that for every P∈𝒜∪ℬP\in\mathscr{A}\cup\mathscr{B}, |A∩P|≈|P|/n|A\cap P|\approx|P|/n.

5. proof of Theorem 4.1

5.1. Inductive construction of 𝒢\mathscr{G}

Let ℱ=(V,E,H,ψ,ϕ)\mathscr{F}=(V,E,H,\psi,\phi). Let n=∑v∈V(g⁡(v)−1)n=\sum\nolimits_{v\in V}(g(v)-1). Initially we let ℱ0=ℱ\mathscr{F}_{0}=\mathscr{F} and g0=gg_{0}=g, and we let Φ0\Phi_{0} be the identity function from VV into VV. Now assume that ℱ0=(V0,E0,H0,ψ0,ϕ0),…,ℱi=(Vi,Ei,Hi,ψi,ϕi)\mathscr{F}_{0}=(V_{0},E_{0},H_{0},\psi_{0},\phi_{0}),\ldots,\mathscr{F}_{i}=(V_{i},E_{i},H_{i},\psi_{i},\phi_{i}) and Φ0,…,Φi\Phi_{0},\ldots,\Phi_{i} have been defined for some i≥0i\geq 0. Also assume that the simple functions g0:V0→ℕ,…,gi:Vi→ℕg_{0}:V_{0}\rightarrow\mathbb{N},\ldots,g_{i}:V_{i}\rightarrow\mathbb{N} have been defined for some i≥0i\geq 0. Let Ψi=Φ0​…​Φi\Psi_{i}=\Phi_{0}\ldots\Phi_{i}. If i=ni=n, we terminate the construction, letting 𝒢=ℱn\mathscr{G}=\mathscr{F}_{n} and Ψ=Ψn\Psi=\Psi_{n}.

If i<ni<n, we can select a vertex α\alpha of ℱi\mathscr{F}_{i} such that gi​(α)≥2g_{i}(\alpha)\geq 2. As we will see, ℱi+1\mathscr{F}_{i+1} is formed from ℱi\mathscr{F}_{i} by splitting off a vertex vi+1v_{i+1} from α\alpha so that we end up with α\alpha and vi+1v_{i+1}. Let

(1) 𝒜i\displaystyle\mathscr{A}_{i} =\displaystyle= {Hℱi​(α)}\displaystyle\{H_{\mathscr{F}_{i}}(\alpha)\}
⋃\displaystyle\bigcup {Hℱi​(1)​(α),…,Hℱi​(k)​(α)}\displaystyle\{H_{\mathscr{F}_{i}(1)}(\alpha),\ldots,H_{\mathscr{F}_{i}(k)}(\alpha)\}
⋃\displaystyle\bigcup {Hℱi​(j)(α,e):e∈Eℱi​(j)(α),1≤j≤k},\displaystyle\{H_{\mathscr{F}_{i}(j)}(\alpha,e):e\in E_{\mathscr{F}_{i}(j)}(\alpha),1\leq j\leq k\},

and let

6. corollaries

For a matrix AA, let AjA_{j} denote the jt​hj^{th} column of AA, and let s⁡(A)s(A) denote the sum of all the elements of AA. Let R=[r1​…​rk]TR=[r_{1}\dots r_{k}]^{T} (or RT=[ri]1×kR^{T}=[r_{i}]_{1\times k}), Λ=[λ1​…​λm]T\Lambda=[\lambda_{1}\dots\lambda_{m}]^{T} and H=[h1​…​hm]TH=[h_{1}\dots h_{m}]^{T} be three column vectors with ri,λi∈ℕr_{i},\lambda_{i}\in{\mathbb{N}}, and hi∈{1,…,n}h_{i}\in\{1,\dots,n\} for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, such that h1​…,hmh_{1}\dots,h_{m} are distinct. Let Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} denote a hypergraph with vertex set VV, |V|=n|V|=n, such that there are λi\lambda_{i} edges of size hih_{i} incident with every hih_{i} vertices for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m. A hypergraph 𝒢\mathscr{G} is said to be kk-regular if every vertex has degree kk. A kk-factor of 𝒢\mathscr{G} is a kk-regular spanning sub-hypergraph of 𝒢\mathscr{G}. An RR-factorization is a partition (decomposition) {F1,…,Fk}\{F_{1},\ldots,F_{k}\} of E⁡(𝒢)E(\mathscr{G}) in which FiF_{i} is an rir_{i}-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. Notice that Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is ∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}-regular. We show that the obvious necessary conditions for the existence of an RR-factorization of Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H}, are also sufficient.

Theorem 6.1.

Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is RR-factorizable if and only if s⁡(R)=∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)s(R)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}, and there exists a non-negative integer matrix A=[ai​j]k×mA=[a_{ij}]_{k\times m} such that A​H=n​RAH=nR, and s⁡(Aj)=λj​(nhj)s(A_{j})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m.1\leq j\leq m.

Proof.

To prove the necessity, suppose that Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is RR-factorizable. Since each rir_{i}-factor is an rir_{i}-regular spanning sub-hypergraph for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, and Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is ∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}-regular, we must have s⁡(R)=∑i=1kri=∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)s(R)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}r_{i}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}. Let ai​ja_{ij} be the number of edges (counting multiplicities) of size hjh_{j} contributing to the it​hi^{th} factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. Since for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, each edge of size hjh_{j} contributes hjh_{j} to the the sum of the degrees of the vertices in an rir_{i}-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, we must have ∑j=1mai​j​hj=n​ri\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{ij}h_{j}=nr_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k and ∑i=1kai​j=λj​(nhj)\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{ij}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m.

To prove the sufficiency, let ℱ\mathscr{F} be a hypergraph consisting of a single vertex vv with mℱ​(vhj)=λj​(nhj)m_{\mathscr{F}}(v^{h_{j}})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. Note that ℱ\mathscr{F} is an amalgamation of Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H}. Now we color the edges of ℱ\mathscr{F} so that mℱ⁡(i)​(vhj)=ai​jm_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v^{h_{j}})=a_{ij} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. This can be done, because:

∑i=1kmℱ⁡(i)​(vhj)=∑i=1kai​j=λj​(nhj)=mℱ​(vhj)​ for ​1≤j≤m.\sum_{i=1}^{k}m_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v^{h_{j}})=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{ij}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}=m_{\mathscr{F}}(v^{h_{j}})\mbox{\quad for }1\leq j\leq m.

Moreover,

dℱ⁡(i)​(v)=∑j=1mai​j​hj=n​ri​ for ​1≤i≤k.d_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{ij}h_{j}=nr_{i}\mbox{ \quad for }1\leq i\leq k.

Let g:V⁡(ℱ)→ℕg:V(\mathscr{F})\rightarrow\mathbb{N} be a function so that g⁡(v)=ng(v)=n. Since for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, hi≤nh_{i}\leq n, gg is simple. By Theorem 4.1, there exists a simple gg-detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} of ℱ\mathscr{F} with nn vertices, say v1,…,vnv_{1},\ldots,v_{n} such that by (A2), d𝒢⁡(i)​(vj)≈dℱ⁡(i)​(v)/g⁡(v)=n​ri/n=rid_{\mathscr{G}(i)}(v_{j})\approx d_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v)/g(v)=nr_{i}/n=r_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤n1\leq j\leq n, and by (A3), for each U⊂{v1,…,vn}U\subset\{v_{1},\dots,v_{n}\} with |U|=hj|U|=h_{j}, m𝒢​(U)≈mℱ​(vhj)/(nhj)=λj​(nhj)/(nhj)=λjm_{\mathscr{G}}(U)\approx m_{\mathscr{F}}(v^{h_{j}})/\binom{n}{h_{j}}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}/\binom{n}{h_{j}}=\lambda_{j} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. Therefore 𝒢≅Λ​KnH\mathscr{G}\cong\Lambda K_{n}^{H}, and the it​hi^{th} color class induces an rir_{i}-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. ∎

In particular, if m=1m=1, h:=h1h:=h_{1}, λ1=1\lambda_{1}=1, r:=r1=⋯=rkr:=r_{1}=\dots=r_{k}, then Theorem 6.1 implies Baranyai’s theorem: the complete hh-uniform hypergraph KnhK_{n}^{h} is rr-factorizable if and only if h∣r​nh\divides rn and r∣(n−1h−1)r\divides\binom{n-1}{h-1}.

Now let hi≥2h_{i}\geq 2 for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, and let Λ​Kp1,…,pnH\Lambda K^{H}_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}} be a hypergraph with vertex partition {V1,…,Vn}\{V_{1},\dots,V_{n}\}, |Vi|=pi|V_{i}|=p_{i} for 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n such that there are λi\lambda_{i} edges of size hih_{i} incident with every hih_{i} vertices, at most one vertex from each part for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m (so no edge is incident with more than one vertex of a part). If p1=⋯=pn:=pp_{1}=\dots=p_{n}:=p, we denote Λ​Kp1,…,pnH\Lambda K^{H}_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}} by Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K^{H}_{n\times p}.

Theorem 6.2.

Λ​Kp1,…,pnH\Lambda K_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}}^{H} is RR-factorizable if and only if p1=⋯=pn:=pp_{1}=\dots=p_{n}:=p, s⁡(R)=∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1s(R)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}, and there exists a non-negative integer matrix A=[ai​j]k×mA=[a_{ij}]_{k\times m} such that A​H=n​p​RAH=npR, and s⁡(Aj)=λj​(nhj)​phjs(A_{j})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}p^{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m.1\leq j\leq m.

Proof.

To prove the necessity, suppose that Λ​Kp1,…,pnH\Lambda K_{p_{1},\dots,p_{n}}^{H} is RR-factorizable (so it is regular). Let uu and vv be two vertices from two different parts, say at​ha^{th} and bt​hb^{th} parts, respectively. Since d⁡(u)=d⁡(v)d(u)=d(v), we have

∑1≤j≤mλj​∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−1≤na∉{i1,…,ihj−1}pi1​…​pihj−1=∑1≤j≤mλj​∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−1≤nb∉{i1,…,ihj−1}pi1​…​pihj−1⇔∑1≤j≤mλj​(∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−1≤na∉{i1,…,ihj−1}pi1​…​pihj−1−∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−1≤nb∉{i1,…,ihj−1}pi1​…​pihj−1)=0⇔∑1≤j≤mλj(pb∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−2≤npi1…pihj−2−pa∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−2≤npi1…pihj−2)=0⇔(pb−pa)∑1≤j≤mλj∑1≤i1<⋯<ihj−2≤npi1…pihj−2=0⇔pb=pa.\begin{split}\sum_{1\leq j\leq m}\lambda_{j}\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\leq n\hfill\atop\scriptstyle a\notin\{i_{1},\dots,i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\}\hfill}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-1}}=\sum_{1\leq j\leq m}\lambda_{j}\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\leq n\hfill\atop\scriptstyle b\notin\{i_{1},\dots,i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\}\hfill}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-1}}&\iff\\ \sum_{1\leq j\leq m}\lambda_{j}\Big(\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\leq n\hfill\atop\scriptstyle a\notin\{i_{1},\dots,i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\}\hfill}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-1}}-\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\leq n\hfill\atop\scriptstyle b\notin\{i_{1},\dots,i_{{}_{h_{j}-1}}\}\hfill}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-1}}\Big)=0&\iff\\ \sum_{1\leq j\leq m}\lambda_{j}\Big(p_{b}\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-2}}\leq n}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-2}}-p_{a}\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-2}}\leq n}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-2}}\Big)=0&\iff\\ (p_{b}-p_{a})\sum_{1\leq j\leq m}\lambda_{j}\sum\nolimits_{\scriptstyle 1\leq i_{1}<\dots<i_{{}_{h_{j}-2}}\leq n}p_{i_{1}}\dots p_{i_{h_{j}-2}}=0&\iff\\ p_{b}=p_{a}.&\end{split}

Therefore, p1=⋯=pn:=pp_{1}=\dots=p_{n}:=p. So Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K^{H}_{n\times p} is ∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}-regular, and we must have s⁡(R)=∑i=1kri=∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1s(R)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}r_{i}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}. Moreover, there must exist non-negative integers ai​ja_{ij}, 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, such that ∑j=1mai​j​hj=n​p​ri\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{ij}h_{j}=npr_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k and ∑i=1kai​j=λj​(nhj)​phj\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{ij}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}p^{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. We note that ai​ja_{ij} is in fact the number of edges (counting multiplicities) of size hjh_{j} contributing to the it​hi^{th} factor.

To prove the sufficiency, let Λp=[phi​λi]1×mT\Lambda^{p}=[p^{h_{i}}\lambda_{i}]_{1\times m}^{T}, and let ℱ=Λp​KnH\mathscr{F}=\Lambda^{p}K^{H}_{n} with vertex set V={v1,…,vn}V=\{v_{1},\dots,v_{n}\}. Notice that ℱ\mathscr{F} is an amalgamation of Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K^{H}_{n\times p}. By Theorem 6.1, ℱ\mathscr{F} is p​RpR-factorizable. Therefore, we can color the edges of ℱ\mathscr{F} so that

dℱ⁡(i)​(v)=p​ri​ for ​v∈V,1≤i≤k.d_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v)=pr_{i}\mbox{ for }v\in V,1\leq i\leq k.

Let g:V→ℕg:V\rightarrow\mathbb{N} be a function so that g⁡(v)=pg(v)=p for v∈Vv\in V. Since p≥1p\geq 1, gg is simple. By Theorem 4.1, there exists a simple gg-detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} of ℱ\mathscr{F} with n​pnp vertices, say viv_{i} is detached to vi​1,…,vi​pv_{i1},\dots,v_{ip} for 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n, such that by (A2), d𝒢⁡(i)​(va​b)≈dℱ⁡(i)​(va)/g⁡(va)=p​ri/p=rid_{\mathscr{G}(i)}(v_{ab})\approx d_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v_{a})/g(v_{a})=pr_{i}/p=r_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤a≤n1\leq a\leq n, 1≤b≤p1\leq b\leq p, and by (A3), m𝒢​(va1​b1,…,vahj​bhj)≈mℱ​(va1,…,vahj)/phj=phj​λj/phj=λjm_{\mathscr{G}}(v_{a_{1}b_{1}},\dots,v_{a_{h_{j}}b_{h_{j}}})\approx m_{\mathscr{F}}(v_{a_{1}},\dots,v_{a_{h_{j}}})/p^{h_{j}}=p^{h_{j}}\lambda_{j}/p^{h_{j}}=\lambda_{j} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, 1≤a1<⋯<ahj≤n1\leq a_{1}<\dots<a_{h_{j}}\leq n, 1≤b1,…,bhj≤p1\leq b_{1},\dots,b_{h_{j}}\leq p. Therefore 𝒢≅Λ​Kn×pH\mathscr{G}\cong\Lambda K^{H}_{n\times p}, and the it​hi^{th} color class induces an rir_{i}-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. ∎

In particular, if m=1m=1, h:=h1h:=h_{1}, λ1=1\lambda_{1}=1, r:=r1=⋯=rkr:=r_{1}=\dots=r_{k}, then Theorem 6.2 implies another one of Baranyai’s theorems: the complete hh-uniform nn-partite hypergraph Kn×phK_{n\times p}^{h} is rr-factorizable if and only if h∣n​p​rh\divides npr and r∣(n−1h−1)​ph−1r\divides\binom{n-1}{h-1}p^{h-1}.

Let JkT=[1​…​1]1×kJ_{k}^{T}=[1\dots 1]_{1\times k}. For two column vectors Q=[q1​…​qk]TQ=[q_{1}\dots q_{k}]^{T}, R=[r1​…​rk]TR=[r_{1}\dots r_{k}]^{T}, if qi≤riq_{i}\leq r_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, we say that Q≤RQ\leq R. For a hypergraph 𝒢\mathscr{G}, a (q,r)(q,r)-factor is a spanning sub-hypergraph in which

q≤d⁡(v)≤r​ for each ​v∈V⁡(𝒢).q\leq d(v)\leq r\mbox{ for each }v\in V(\mathscr{G}).

A (Q,R)(Q,R)-factorization is a partition {F1,…,Fk}\{F_{1},\ldots,F_{k}\} of E⁡(𝒢)E(\mathscr{G}) in which FiF_{i} is a (qi,ri)(q_{i},r_{i})-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. An almost kk-factor of 𝒢\mathscr{G} is (k−1,k)(k-1,k)-factor. An almost RR-factorization is an (R−Jk,R)(R-J_{k},R)-factorization. The proof of the following theorems are very similar to those of Theorem 6.1 and 6.2.

Theorem 6.3.

Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is (Q,R)(Q,R)-factorizable if and only if s⁡(Q)≤∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)≤s⁡(R)s(Q)\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}\leq s(R), and there exists a non-negative integer matrix A=[ai​j]k×mA=[a_{ij}]_{k\times m} such that n​Q≤A​H≤n​RnQ\leq AH\leq nR, and s⁡(Aj)=λj​(nhj)s(A_{j})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m.

Proof.

To prove the necessity, suppose that Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is (Q,R)(Q,R)-factorizable. Since Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is ∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}-regular, we must have s⁡(Q)=∑i=1kqi≤∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)≤∑i=1kri=s⁡(R)s(Q)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}q_{i}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{k}r_{i}=s(R). Since for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, each edge of size hjh_{j} contributes hjh_{j} to the the sum of the degrees of the vertices in (qi,ri)(q_{i},r_{i})-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, there must exist non-negative integers ai​ja_{ij}, 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, such that n​qi≤∑j=1mai​j​hj≤n​rinq_{i}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{ij}h_{j}\leq nr_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k and ∑i=1kai​j=λj​(nhj)\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{ij}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m.

To prove the sufficiency, let ℱ\mathscr{F} be a hypergraph consisting of a single vertex vv with mℱ​(vhj)=λj​(nhj)m_{\mathscr{F}}(v^{h_{j}})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. Note that ℱ\mathscr{F} is an amalgamation of Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H}. Now we color the edges of ℱ\mathscr{F} so that mℱ⁡(i)​(vhj)=ai​jm_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v^{h_{j}})=a_{ij} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. This can be done, because:

∑i=1kmℱ⁡(i)​(vhj)=∑i=1kai​j=λj​(nhj)=mℱ​(vhj)​ for ​1≤j≤m.\sum_{i=1}^{k}m_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v^{h_{j}})=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{ij}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}=m_{\mathscr{F}}(v^{h_{j}})\mbox{\quad for }1\leq j\leq m.

Moreover,

n​qi≤dℱ⁡(i)​(v)=∑j=1mai​j​hj≤n​ri​ for ​1≤i≤k.nq_{i}\leq d_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{ij}h_{j}\leq nr_{i}\mbox{ \quad for }1\leq i\leq k.

Let g:V⁡(ℱ)→ℕg:V(\mathscr{F})\rightarrow\mathbb{N} be a function so that g⁡(v)=ng(v)=n. Since for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, hi≤nh_{i}\leq n, gg is simple. By Theorem 4.1, there exists a simple gg-detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} of ℱ\mathscr{F} with nn vertices, say v1,…,vnv_{1},\ldots,v_{n} such that by (A2), qi=n​qi/n≤d𝒢⁡(i)​(vj)≤n​ri/n=riq_{i}=nq_{i}/n\leq d_{\mathscr{G}(i)}(v_{j})\leq nr_{i}/n=r_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤n1\leq j\leq n, and by (A3), for each U⊂{v1,…,vn}U\subset\{v_{1},\dots,v_{n}\} with |U|=hj|U|=h_{j}, m𝒢​(U)≈mℱ​(vhj)/(nhj)=λj​(nhj)/(nhj)=λjm_{\mathscr{G}}(U)\approx m_{\mathscr{F}}(v^{h_{j}})/\binom{n}{h_{j}}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}/\binom{n}{h_{j}}=\lambda_{j} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m. Therefore 𝒢≅Λ​KnH\mathscr{G}\cong\Lambda K_{n}^{H}, and the it​hi^{th} color class induces a (qi,ri)(q_{i},r_{i})-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. ∎

Theorem 6.4.

Λ​KnH\Lambda K_{n}^{H} is almost RR-factorizable if and only if s⁡(R)−k≤∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)≤s⁡(R)s(R)-k\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}\leq s(R), and there exists a non-negative integer matrix A=[ai​j]k×mA=[a_{ij}]_{k\times m} such that n⁡(R−Jk)≤A​H≤n​Rn(R-J_{k})\leq AH\leq nR, and s⁡(Aj)=λj​(nhj)s(A_{j})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m.

Proof.

It is enough to take Q=R−JkQ=R-J_{k} in Theorem 6.3. ∎

Theorem 6.5.

Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K_{n\times p}^{H} is (Q,R)(Q,R)-factorizable if and only if s⁡(Q)≤∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1≤s⁡(R)s(Q)\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}\leq s(R), and there exists a non-negative integer matrix A=[ai​j]k×mA=[a_{ij}]_{k\times m} such that n​p​Q≤A​H≤n​p​RnpQ\leq AH\leq npR, and s⁡(Aj)=λj​(nhj)​phjs(A_{j})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}p^{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m.1\leq j\leq m.

Proof.

To prove the necessity, suppose that Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K_{n\times p}^{H} is (Q,R)(Q,R)-factorizable. Since Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K_{n\times p}^{H} is ∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}-regular, we must have s⁡(Q)=∑i=1kqi≤∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1≤∑i=1kri=s⁡(R)s(Q)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}q_{i}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{k}r_{i}=s(R). Moreover, there must exist non-negative integers ai​ja_{ij}, 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, such that n​p​qi≤∑j=1mai​j​hj≤n​p​rinpq_{i}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{ij}h_{j}\leq npr_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k and ∑i=1kai​j=λj​(nhj)​phj\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{ij}=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}p^{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m.

To prove the sufficiency, let Λp=[phi​λi]1×mT\Lambda^{p}=[p^{h_{i}}\lambda_{i}]_{1\times m}^{T}, and let ℱ=Λp​KnH\mathscr{F}=\Lambda^{p}K^{H}_{n} with vertex set V={v1,…,vn}V=\{v_{1},\dots,v_{n}\}. Notice that ℱ\mathscr{F} is an amalgamation of Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K^{H}_{n\times p}. By Theorem 6.3, ℱ\mathscr{F} is (p​Q,p​R)(pQ,pR)-factorizable. Therefore, we can color the edges of ℱ\mathscr{F} so that

p​qi≤dℱ⁡(i)​(v)≤p​ri​ for ​v∈V,1≤i≤k.pq_{i}\leq d_{\mathscr{F}(i)}(v)\leq pr_{i}\mbox{ for }v\in V,1\leq i\leq k.

Let g:V→ℕg:V\rightarrow\mathbb{N} be a function so that g⁡(v)=pg(v)=p for v∈Vv\in V. Since p≥1p\geq 1, gg is simple. By Theorem 4.1, there exists a simple gg-detachment 𝒢\mathscr{G} of ℱ\mathscr{F} with n​pnp vertices, say viv_{i} is detached to vi​1,…,vi​pv_{i1},\dots,v_{ip} for 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n, such that by (A2), qi=p​qi/p≤d𝒢⁡(i)​(va​b)≤p​ri/p=riq_{i}=pq_{i}/p\leq d_{\mathscr{G}(i)}(v_{ab})\leq pr_{i}/p=r_{i} for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k, 1≤a≤n1\leq a\leq n, 1≤b≤p1\leq b\leq p, and by (A3), m𝒢​(va1​b1,…,vahj​bhj)≈mℱ​(va1,…,vahj)/phj=phj​λj/phj=λjm_{\mathscr{G}}(v_{a_{1}b_{1}},\dots,v_{a_{h_{j}}b_{h_{j}}})\approx m_{\mathscr{F}}(v_{a_{1}},\dots,v_{a_{h_{j}}})/p^{h_{j}}=p^{h_{j}}\lambda_{j}/p^{h_{j}}=\lambda_{j} for 1≤j≤m1\leq j\leq m, 1≤a1<⋯<ahj≤n1\leq a_{1}<\dots<a_{h_{j}}\leq n, 1≤b1,…,bhj≤p1\leq b_{1},\dots,b_{h_{j}}\leq p. Therefore 𝒢≅Λ​Kn×pH\mathscr{G}\cong\Lambda K^{H}_{n\times p}, and the it​hi^{th} color class induces a (pi,ri)(p_{i},r_{i})-factor for 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. ∎

Theorem 6.6.

Λ​Kn×pH\Lambda K_{n\times p}^{H} is almost RR-factorizable if and only if s⁡(R)−k≤∑i=1mλi​(n−1hi−1)​phi−1≤s⁡(R)s(R)-k\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_{i}\binom{n-1}{h_{i}-1}p^{h_{i}-1}\leq s(R), and there exists a non-negative integer matrix A=[ai​j]k×mA=[a_{ij}]_{k\times m} such that n​p​(R−Jk)≤A​H≤n​p​Rnp(R-J_{k})\leq AH\leq npR, and s⁡(Aj)=λj​(nhj)​phjs(A_{j})=\lambda_{j}\binom{n}{h_{j}}p^{h_{j}} for 1≤j≤m.1\leq j\leq m.

Proof.

It is enough to take Q=R−JkQ=R-J_{k} in Theorem 6.5. ∎
